relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: She studied medieval music at Durham University

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: and then received a scholarship to Trinity College of Music in London, England.

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: she arrived at Sojiji to study Soto Zen Buddhism under him... Formally, Kōho Keidō Chisan Zenji was her teacher

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: practically, one of Keido Zenji's senior officers, Suigan Yogo roshi, was her main instructor

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: Before leaving for Japan, Kennett was ordained a novice nun by Venerable Seck Kim Seng (釋金星; Shì Jīnxīng) in the Linji Chan school

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: Following her Zuise ceremony, Jiyu-Kennett was installed as shinzan (head priest) of Unpukuji temple in Mie prefecture.

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: In 1969, Jiyu-Kennett founded the Zen Mission Society in San Francisco

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: and in 1970 Shasta Abbey in Mount Shasta, California, the first Zen monastery in the United States to be established by a woman.

relations.subject: Hōun Jiyu-Kennett
relations.evidence: she resigned from her position as abbess of Shasta Abbey... and again assumed her position as Abbess of Shasta Abbey for the next 20 years until her death on November 6, 1996.

relations.subject: Daizui MacPhillamy
relations.evidence: she had her student Daizui MacPhillamy with her often to tend to her care. Following a kensho experience he had, she conferred Dharma transmission to him at her bedside in 1976.
